register.name: Strengthening Fiscal Resilience for Sustainable Development Program, Subprogram 2
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · 57121-002 · approved July 2026 · concessional loan · cofinanced by New Zealand (US$1.17 million)
register.note: Completes a programme that has reduced public debt and rebuilt fiscal buffers
register.text: An ADB concessional loan that completes a programme supporting Palau’s fiscal resilience, which has reduced public debt, strengthened revenue collection and rebuilt fiscal buffers, and set up a Debt and Investment Office, funds to cushion the economy against downturns and disasters, and a National Planning Office. It strengthens the public finances that carry the seven standards.

register.name: Koror–Airai Sanitation Project, grant cofinancing
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · Urban Resilience Trust Fund · 2025 · to complete the remaining work of the project
register.note: The tender to complete pump stations SPS1 and SPS2 ran from January to May 2025
register.text: A $2 million grant from the Urban Resilience Trust Fund, through ADB, to complete the remaining work of the Koror–Airai Sanitation Project, which is rebuilding the sewer networks and pump stations of Koror, Malakal and Meyuns. Safe sanitation serves the shelter, water and health standards.

register.name: Clean energy access, additional financing
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · committed 2024 · Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism · through the National Development Bank of Palau
register.note: Lent on through the National Development Bank of Palau
register.text: Additional ADB financing from the Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism to give communities access to clean energy and to accelerate clean energy investment through the National Development Bank of Palau. It serves the energy standard.
by: Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism

register.name: Strengthening Fiscal Resilience for Sustainable Development Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · approved 2024 · programmatic approach · loan to enhance fiscal discipline
register.note: The first of two loans; the second, of the same size, followed in July 2026
register.text: An ADB loan under a programmatic approach to enhance fiscal discipline, the first stage of the fiscal resilience programme completed in 2026. It strengthens the public finances that carry the seven standards.

register.name: Compact of Free Association, economic assistance
register.detail: United States · Compact of Free Association Amendments Act of 2024 · in force March 2024 · through 2043 · fiscal year 2027: more than $41 million, announced 12 November 2026
register.text: Twenty years of US grant assistance and trust fund contributions to Palau under the renewed Compact, through 2043; $6.5 billion in all for Micronesia, the Marshall Islands and Palau. For fiscal year 2027, the Department of the Interior announced more than $41 million for Palau for health care, education, infrastructure, the Infrastructure Maintenance Fund and the Fiscal Consolidation Fund.
register.note: All three nations: $6.5 billion over 20 years

register.name: Development loan for the local economy
register.detail: Saudi Fund for Development · signed in Ngerulmud, April 2026 · channelled through the National Development Bank of Palau
register.note: The President named affordable, climate-resilient housing as a priority
register.text: A US$15 million development loan from the Saudi Fund for Development, channelled through the National Development Bank of Palau, for projects led by Palauan developers, businesses and entrepreneurs. Affordable, climate-resilient housing is among its stated priorities, serving the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Energy support grant, Economic and Social Development Programme
register.detail: Government of Japan · Exchange of Notes signed 9 February 2026 · up to ¥300 million (about $2 million) · power sector
register.note: About $2 million, for a reliable energy source in the power sector
register.text: A Japanese grant of up to 300 million yen, about $2 million, under the Economic and Social Development Programme, to ensure a reliable energy source for the smooth operation and sustainability of Palau’s power sector. It serves the energy standard.
